response.justification: Broad, senior-level engineer with a current Staff title and directly relevant hands-on exposure to agentic tooling (MCP code generators, AI-agent infrastructure), plus genuine high-throughput distributed systems experience at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (millions of HTTP req/s, async I/O, caching, low-latency services). TypeScript/Node depth is strong and well above the 'working level' bar. The main gaps are the absence of Python anywhere in the resume despite it being a must-have, distributed-systems depth that is concentrated in a 2018–2020 role rather than recent work, and thin evidence of the non-technical staff-level expectations — technical strategy at scale, cross-functional stakeholder management, and formal on-call/incident ownership. Worth a screen to probe Python proficiency and scope of influence, but not an unambiguous yes on paper.
strengths: Hands-on agentic/AI tooling work (MCP generators, agent frameworks) matches the AI-native baseline
Proven high-throughput, low-latency microservices experience at ad-tech scale
Deep TypeScript/Node plus strong craftsmanship signals (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based, open-source test tooling)
concerns: Python — a must-have — is not listed or evidenced anywhere
Distributed-systems depth is dated (2018–2020); recent roles skew product/full-stack
Little evidence of technical strategy at scale, stakeholder management, or on-call/incident ownership
